'''John Herbert Watkinson''' (27 August 1932 – 14 February 2017) was a New Zealand soil chemist.

Watkinson studied at [[Victoria University of Wellington|Victoria University College]], graduating with a [[BSc]] in 1953.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university24.html |title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: U–Wh |date= |website= |publisher= |accessdate=16 February 2017 }}</ref> He later completed a [[PhD]] at the same institution in 1969, following its attainment of autonomy as [[Victoria University of Wellington]]. His thesis, supervised by Alex Wilson, was titled ''The kinetics of ion exchange in soil''.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://tewaharoa.victoria.ac.nz/VUW:64VUW_ALL:64VUW_INST21132007050002386 | title=The kinetics of ion exchange in soil | publisher=Victoria University of Wellington Library | accessdate=16 February 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | url=http://www.victoria.ac.nz/scps/about/attachments/ChemHist_second-edition_lowres.pdf | title=Chemistry at Victoria: the Wellington university | page=147 | first=Brian | last=Halton | authorlink=Brian Halton | edition=2 | year=2014 | isbn=978-0-475-12408-1 | publisher=Victoria University of Wellington | accessdate=16 February 2017}}</ref> Watkinson worked at the Ruakura Agricultural Research Centre,<ref \>{{cite web | url=http://tracenz.org/conference1977/NZTEG_1977_002_Branch_Members.pdf | title=Members of the trace elements and health research group of New Zealand | year=1977 | publisher=New Zealand Trace Elements Group | accessdate=16 February 2017 | archive-date=16 February 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170216220118/http://tracenz.org/conference1977/NZTEG_1977_002_Branch_Members.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref> and he is noted for developing the [[Fluorescence spectroscopy|fluorometric determination]] of [[Selenium in biology|selenium]] in biological samples,<ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=p5LkBwAAQBAJ | title=Reactive Oxygen Species in Chemistry, Biology, and Medicine | editor-last=Quintanilha | editor-first=A. | page=23 | publisher=Springer Science & Business Media | location=New York | year=1988 | isbn=978-1-4757-0419-8 | accessdate=16 February 2017}}</ref> and his research into selenium fertilisers and the determination of the optimum particle sizes for elemental sulphur and reactive phosphate rock.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.groupone.co.nz/quinformation-2/fertiliser/challenges-and-innovations-in-fertiliser-technology-and-spreading/ | title=Challenges and innovations in fertiliser technology and spreading | publisher=Group One Consultancy | accessdate=16 February 2017 | archive-date=16 February 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170216221136/http://www.groupone.co.nz/quinformation-2/fertiliser/challenges-and-innovations-in-fertiliser-technology-and-spreading/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 1994, and was also a Fellow of the New Zealand Institute for Advanced Studies.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://royalsociety.org.nz/organisation/academy/fellowship/fellows-1919-present/v-z/ |title=The Academy: V–Z |date= |website= |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |accessdate=16 February 2017}}</ref> His chief laboratory chemist at Ruakura was Grant Ardern who later continued his own career in healthcare informatics. John was married to June Watkinson.

Watkinson died aged 84 in [[Hamilton, New Zealand|Hamilton]] on 14 February 2017.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://notices.nzherald.co.nz/obituaries/nzherald-nz/obituary.aspx?n=john-herbert-watkinson&pid=184142010 | title=John Watkinson death notice | work=[[New Zealand Herald]] | date=16 February 2017 | accessdate=16 February 2017}}</ref>
